countries.name: Romania
countries.summary: Romania is an EU member state with a long tradition of medical education, home to several state medical universities that have run dedicated English-medium Medicine programmes for international students for decades. Its degrees carry automatic recognition across the EU/EEA under Directive 2005/36/EC.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: Romania combines EU-recognized, direct-entry six-year Medicine degrees with an established international student community, English-medium instruction at multiple state universities, and tuition well below most Western European destinations.
countries.climate: Temperate continental climate with warm summers and cold, snowy winters, typical of Central-Eastern Europe.
countries.metaTitle: Study MBBS and Medicine in Romania
countries.metaDescription: Explore English-medium MBBS and Medicine programs in Romania, including admissions, fees, EU recognition and accommodation guidance for international students.

universities.name: Iuliu Hatieganu University of Medicine and Pharmacy
universities.summary: Iuliu Hatieganu University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Cluj-Napoca runs a direct-entry, six-year English-medium Medicine programme leading to the Doctor Medic degree. The university is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, and the Romanian medical qualification carries automatic recognition across the EU/EEA under Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V.
universities.campusLifestyle: International students join a long-established English-medium Medicine cohort alongside a parallel French-medium track, based on the university's main Cluj-Napoca campus, with a separate extension campus in Novara, Italy operating under its own fee schedule for students who choose that route.
universities.cityProfile: Cluj-Napoca is Romania's second-largest city and the unofficial capital of Transylvania, a major university hub with a large resident student population. The city has an international airport with European connections and an established base of foreign medical students built up over several decades.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS Medicine programme combines preclinical foundation years (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, microbiology) with later clinical training in Cluj-Napoca's teaching hospitals, culminating in the Doctor Medic degree, a Romanian medical qualification with automatic EU/EEA recognition under Directive 2005/36/EC.
universities.hostelOverview: The university operates student dormitories on its Hasdeu and Observator campuses, though its published dormitory-fee page reflects an outdated 2023-2024 cycle rather than a current figure. A university-affiliated recruitment portal estimates total average student living costs, including rent, utilities and food, at roughly EUR 600-800 per month; applicants should confirm current dormitory rates directly with the university before budgeting.
universities.dietarySupport: Campus and nearby student cafeterias serve the university community; no separate university-run meal-plan cost is published.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research. Admissions and student queries are handled through the university's International Relations Office.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants apply and track their file through the university's own online admissions platform, with correspondence handled by the International Relations Office in Cluj-Napoca.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0001415) under its Faculty of Medicine record.
The Doctor Medic qualification sits on Romania's EU Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V automatic-recognition list (reference date 1 January 2007), applicable across the EU/EEA.
Direct-entry six-year, 360-ECTS Medicine programme open to students straight from an accredited secondary school, with no prior degree required.
Officially confirmed current 2026/27 tuition of EUR 10,000 for Year 1, published in a dated university fee schedule alongside the live admissions page.
Long-established English-medium track (also available in French) at a state medical university founded in 1919, with Cluj's Faculty of Medicine tracing back to 1776.
thingsToConsider: The university's official admissions page currently shows a live extended deadline of 12 August 2026 for the English Medicine track, which differs from its own published Session II calendar ending 16 July 2026 -- confirm the operative deadline directly with the university before applying.

WDOMS separately notes 'an entrance exam is required' for this school, which appears to conflict with the university's own file-evaluation-based international admissions route; this discrepancy was not resolved during research.

No specific numeric English-test score (such as an IELTS or TOEFL band) is published on the official admissions page -- only a general minimum B2 CEFR requirement, with several stated exemption routes.
The university's own dormitory-fee page has not been updated past the 2023-2024 cycle, so no current on-campus housing cost could be confirmed.
A separate Novara, Italy extension campus for Medicine exists under its own distinct fee schedule (EUR 14,800 for Year 1); this record covers the Cluj-Napoca campus only.
bestFitFor: Students seeking a direct-entry, EU-recognized six-year Medicine degree at a lower tuition point than most Western European destinations.
Applicants comfortable navigating an online, file-evaluation-based admissions process without a standardized written entrance exam.
Students who have independently arranged or budgeted for off-campus housing, given the lack of a confirmed current dormitory rate.

faq.question: Is the English Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Admission requires completion of an accredited high school whose diploma grants access to university studies in the applicant's home country; no prior university degree is required.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Doctor Medic degree, a Romanian medical qualification listed under EU Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V for automatic recognition across the EU/EEA.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 10,000 per year for Years 1 and 2, reducing in later years (Year 3: EUR 8,500; Year 4: EUR 8,000; Years 5-6: EUR 7,500 each), totaling EUR 51,500 across the 6-year programme, confirmed for the 2026/27 academic year in the university's official fee schedule.

faq.question: Is there a separate application fee?
faq.answer: Yes. A non-refundable EUR 300 processing fee applies, plus a confirmation-of-place payment equal to 50% of the tuition fee once admitted, with the remainder payable by bank transfer.

faq.question: What English-proficiency proof is required?
faq.answer: A minimum B2 CEFR-level English certificate not older than the university's stated validity window, unless the applicant completed secondary schooling in English or achieved B2-equivalent English in their baccalaureate exam.

faq.question: Is there a written entrance exam?
faq.answer: The university's own official admissions page describes an evaluation-based international admissions route without a written exam, though the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools separately lists an entrance exam as required -- applicants should confirm the current process directly with the university.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: Enrollment for admitted students takes place in the last two weeks of September. As of this record's research date, the university's live admissions page showed an extended application deadline of 12 August 2026 for the English Medicine track.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: The university operates dormitories on its Hasdeu and Observator campuses, but its published dormitory-fee page reflects an outdated cycle rather than a current rate; confirm current cost directly with the university.

faq.question: Can this degree be used to practice medicine outside Romania?
faq.answer: The Doctor Medic qualification carries automatic recognition across the EU/EEA under Directive 2005/36/EC. For India specifically, graduates would need to separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission screening requirements; this was not independently verified against an NMC source during research.
